title: Rate Limiting
overview: Rate limiting controls how many requests a client can make to a service within a time window. It protects APIs from abuse, prevents server overload, ensures fair usage across consumers, and provides a first line of defense against DDoS attacks. Rate limits are typically enforced at the API gateway or reverse proxy layer.
keyPoints: Protects services from abuse, overload, and denial-of-service attacks
Ensures fair resource allocation across all API consumers
Rate limit responses use 429 Too Many Requests status code
Limits can be per user, per IP, per API key, or per endpoint
Distributed rate limiting requires shared state (Redis) across multiple gateway instances
Communicate limits via headers: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, Retry-After

concepts.name: Token Bucket
concepts.description: A bucket holds N tokens. Each request consumes one token. Tokens replenish at a fixed rate. Allows short bursts up to bucket capacity. Most common algorithm.

concepts.name: Leaky Bucket
concepts.description: Requests enter a queue (bucket) and are processed at a fixed output rate — excess requests overflow and are rejected. Enforces strict, smooth output rate. No bursting.

concepts.name: Fixed Window Counter
concepts.description: Counts requests per fixed time window (e.g., 100 req/min). Simple but vulnerable to boundary bursts — 100 requests at 00:59 + 100 at 01:00 = 200 in 2 seconds.

concepts.name: Sliding Window Log
concepts.description: Stores a timestamp log of recent requests. Checks if the count within the sliding window exceeds the limit. Accurate but memory-intensive for high traffic.

concepts.name: Sliding Window Counter
concepts.description: Approximates sliding window using weighted combination of current and previous fixed-window counts. Good balance of accuracy and efficiency.

tools.name: Redis
tools.description: Central rate limit state store using atomic INCR + EXPIRE or Lua scripts for correctness

tools.name: Kong
tools.description: API gateway with built-in rate limiting plugin supporting multiple strategies

tools.name: AWS API Gateway
tools.description: Built-in usage plans and API keys with configurable throttling per stage and method

tools.name: Nginx
tools.description: limit_req_zone directive for IP-based rate limiting at the reverse proxy layer

tradeoffs: Rate limiting adds a small latency overhead (especially with distributed Redis-based state). Stricter limits protect servers but may frustrate legitimate users during traffic spikes. Consider implementing tiered limits (free vs. paid users) and providing helpful error messages with Retry-After headers so clients can back off gracefully.
interviewTips: Token bucket is the most common algorithm — explain it clearly with the bucket analogy
Discuss distributed rate limiting — a single API gateway instance can use local counters, but multiple instances need shared Redis state
Mention 429 status code and Retry-After header — good API citizens always return these
Rate limiting is often combined with circuit breakers and load shedding for defense in depth
